summary: 1830 is a heavy 18xx train and stock game where players alternate between buying and dumping shares in railroad companies and physically operating those companies on a hex map to build track and run trains for revenue. The real game is almost entirely economic: timing a stock sale to tank a rival's company, forcing someone into a presidency they can't afford to run, and squeezing every dollar out of train routes.
praised: deep, purely skill-based stock manipulation with no randomness
tense economic decisions and company presidency fights
considered a genre-defining classic of the 18xx family
criticised: steep learning curve and unforgiving of mistakes
significant downtime watching other players' operating rounds
can produce spiteful or kingmaking moves late game

interaction.detail: All players build track and run trains on one shared hexagonal map, so claiming a hex or laying a tile can cut off an opponent's route or station slot. The bigger interaction is through a shared stock market: players buy and sell shares in the same companies, and a company's president (majority holder) makes decisions that affect all its other shareholders.

scoring.how_you_win: You alternate buying/selling railroad stock with operating the companies you control to lay track and run trains for revenue; when the bank runs out of money the game ends and whoever has the greatest total net worth (cash plus share value) wins.
